title: Rectangle Overlap
statement: Return true if two axis-aligned rectangles with positive area overlap.
explanation: Their horizontal intervals and vertical intervals must each overlap with strictly positive length.

title: Magic Squares In Grid
statement: Count 3x3 subgrids that form a 3x3 magic square using the numbers 1 through 9 exactly once.
explanation: Check the center is 5, all values are unique and in 1..9, and all rows, columns, and diagonals sum to 15.

title: Backspace String Compare
statement: Return whether two strings are equal after each # removes the previous available character.
explanation: Build the effective string by pushing ordinary characters and popping on # when possible.

title: Maximize Distance to Closest Person
statement: Return the maximum distance to the nearest occupied seat when choosing one empty seat.
explanation: Consider leading and trailing empty runs and half the length of each interior gap.

title: Peak Index in a Mountain Array
statement: Return the peak index of a mountain array that strictly increases and then strictly decreases.
explanation: If nums[mid] is less than nums[mid+1], the peak lies to the right; otherwise it lies at mid or left.

title: Buddy Strings
approach: Check duplicates or two swapped positions
statement: Return true if swapping exactly two characters in s can make it equal to goal.
explanation: Lengths must match; equal strings need a duplicate character, while unequal strings must differ at exactly two swapped positions.

title: Lemonade Change
approach: Prefer giving a ten and five
statement: Return true if every customer can receive correct change for a $5 lemonade given bills of $5, $10, and $20.
explanation: Track fives and tens; for a $20 bill use a ten plus a five when possible, otherwise three fives.

title: Transpose Matrix
statement: Return the transpose of a matrix by turning each row into a column.
explanation: Create a matrix with reversed dimensions and assign result[c][r] = matrix[r][c].

title: Binary Gap
statement: Return the largest distance between consecutive 1 bits in a positive integer’s binary representation.
explanation: Scan bits from least significant to most significant and measure distances between consecutive set-bit positions.

title: Leaf-Similar Trees
statement: Return true if two trees have the same left-to-right sequence of leaf values.
explanation: Collect leaves in left-to-right DFS order for each tree and compare the sequences.
